name: join_many_to_one
comment: Join-mode eager loading of a many-to-one: the root aliases t and every column re-aliases <alias>_<column> so segment readers partition the row; the join aliases j0 and its ON pairs target = parent; root predicates and orderings qualify with t.

sqlite.sql: select t.id as t_id, t.user_id as t_user_id, t.status as t_status, t.amount as t_amount, t.version as t_version, t.note as t_note, t.created_at as t_created_at, t.updated_at as t_updated_at, j0.id as j0_id, j0.name as j0_name, j0.email as j0_email, j0.display_name as j0_display_name, j0.created_at as j0_created_at, j0.updated_at as j0_updated_at from transactions t left join users j0 on j0.id = t.user_id where t.status = @c0 order by t.id

sqlserver.sql: select t.[id] as [t_id], t.[user_id] as [t_user_id], t.[status] as [t_status], t.[amount] as [t_amount], t.[version] as [t_version], t.[note] as [t_note], t.[created_at] as [t_created_at], t.[updated_at] as [t_updated_at], j0.[id] as [j0_id], j0.[name] as [j0_name], j0.[email] as [j0_email], j0.[display_name] as [j0_display_name], j0.[created_at] as [j0_created_at], j0.[updated_at] as [j0_updated_at] from [transactions] t left join [users] j0 on j0.[id] = t.[user_id] where t.[status] = @c0 order by t.[id]

postgres.sql: select t."id" as "t_id", t."user_id" as "t_user_id", t."status" as "t_status", t."amount" as "t_amount", t."version" as "t_version", t."note" as "t_note", t."created_at" as "t_created_at", t."updated_at" as "t_updated_at", j0."id" as "j0_id", j0."name" as "j0_name", j0."email" as "j0_email", j0."display_name" as "j0_display_name", j0."created_at" as "j0_created_at", j0."updated_at" as "j0_updated_at" from "transactions" t left join "users" j0 on j0."id" = t."user_id" where t."status" = @c0 order by t."id"
